body:
As an offshoot from https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2693 :

4.3.4 is likely being moved to L2.

I suggest moving 4.3.4 into 4.1.3 and 4.1.6 or keep 4.3.4 at L1.

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **4.3.4** | [ADDED] Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions to interact. | 1 > 2 |

... into ...

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **4.1.3** | [MODIFIED, COVERS 4.1.2] Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions. | 1 | 
| **4.1.6** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 4.2.1, COVERS 13.1.4] Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA). | 1 | 

The reason why I am struggling with this and want to somehow keep it at L1 is because 4.3.4 always takes additional access control development work beyond 4.1.3 and 4.1.6. When it's needed, it's extra work that if avoided, is a very high impact mass-data-loss event.

comments.body: For this proposal it makes sense to re-investigate arguments in #2060 and if needed then re-open it.

My point there was this:

> As I said, I believe that it is is important to specifically mention multi-tenancy separation as it might require additional or more stringent controls compared to regular BOLA protection. I think [Jim's comment](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2060#issuecomment-2331769230) nicely illustrates the associated complexities :) We probably don't want to go into as much detail but I think it demonstrates the point.

I think that was the key drive behind having this requirement separate.

> The reason why I am struggling with this and want to somehow keep it at L1 is because 4.3.4 always takes additional access control development work beyond 4.1.3 and 4.1.6. When it's needed, it's extra work that if avoided, is a very high impact mass-data-loss event.

I see the logic here and this is a certain hard-choice but multi-tenancy is something that will affect some apps whereas the basic access control stuff will be relevant for all apps  which is a key factor in why the former was pushed to L2 and the latter is L1.
I think you both made good arguments. I surrender multi-tenancy to L2.
